$comment: Every architecture rule Broiler.VM names, with how much it currently proves.
Milestone VM-1's exit gate asks that the contract be implemented and proven against the
fixture profile. A rule can be expressed long before the checkout contains anything able to
violate it, and a register that did not say so would let a passing suite read as stronger
evidence than it is. Roadmap section 16 makes an untruthful support claim a stop condition and
the status ledger's update rule 4 forbids promoting a shell result, so every rule carries its
status and the evidence bundle repeats the counts.
ONE CRITERION, APPLIED TO EVERY ROW. `status` describes the GRAPH: can anything in the current
checkout violate this rule? `witness` records a real violating input, and every rule has one
regardless of status - a Vacuous rule is one nothing in the component can break, not one that
was never shown working.
Status values, and nothing else: Active, Vacuous, Deferred.
Active   - something in the checkout could violate it, and a witness shows it rejecting one.
Vacuous  - it runs and is witnessed, but nothing in the graph can violate it. Not a defect:
the honest state of a rule whose subject cannot yet be broken.
Deferred - not asserted; the activation milestone owns promoting it.
A Deferred or Vacuous row may never name an activation milestone at or before the current
milestone, and a rule whose activation milestone IS the current milestone must be Active with a
passing witness. RuleRegisterTests enforces the register against the test methods and the
witness inputs in both directions.
WHAT VM-1 CHANGED. Five of the six rows that named VM-1 as their activation milestone are
promoted: the product graph now has method bodies, assembly references and an exported surface,
so B2, B4, B5b, B6 and B7 each have something that could break them. B3 is the one row where
the honest answer is different, and it is recorded rather than papered over - see its own row.
Rule E5 is superseded: it fused a cardinality claim about the graph with a member claim about
one type, and only the first is falsified by VM-1. V1 replaces the first; V2 preserves the
second verbatim.

REVIEW PASS. An adversarial review after the first implementation returned 45 findings that survived refutation, 16 of them blockers. Two register rows were among them: V4 checked a property count rather than the frozen rows it claimed to check, and V9 asserted static return types rather than the construction site. Both statements and both rules were corrected here. A rule weaker than its own statement is the defect this register exists to prevent, so those two are recorded rather than quietly tightened.

rules.statement: No ProjectReference, resolved to a full path, lies outside the component root.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Any project file exists; the outbound half of the legacy boundary.

rules.statement: No PackageReference names a Broiler.* package.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Any project file exists; closes the feed-shaped reintroduction A1 cannot see.

rules.statement: No Compile, None, Content, EmbeddedResource or Import item resolves outside the component root.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Non-vacuous when any project declares one of the five item types; at VM-0 none does, so the sweep is empty and both witnesses carry the rule.

rules.statement: No product project has a ProjectReference resolving under src/tests/.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Broiler.VM.Fixtures exists at VM-0, so the forbidden target is present.

rules.statement: Every project under src/tests/ contains the literal element IsPackable false.
rules.evidence: Project file text, not the evaluated property
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Broiler.VM.Fixtures matches no name-suffix rule in the vendored packaging props and would otherwise default to packable.

rules.statement: Exactly three projects declare a PackageId, and for each PackageId equals AssemblyName equals RootNamespace equals the project file base name.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Three packable projects exist at VM-0.

rules.statement: The resolved ProjectReference edge multiset equals graph.manifest.json exactly; extra and missing edges both fail. Subsumes acyclicity.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Eight edges exist at VM-0.

rules.statement: No profile project references Broiler.VM.Runtime.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Broiler.VM.Fixtures is profile-shaped and exists at VM-0.

rules.statement: Broiler.VM.Runtime declares OutputType Library or omits it, and declares no composition root.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Broiler.VM.Runtime exists at VM-0.

rules.statement: No product project declares InternalsVisibleTo. VM-3 must prove a profile is writable through the public source contract alone.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Three product projects exist at VM-0.

rules.statement: No project outside the composition-root allow-list references an assembly matching Broiler.VM.Profile.*. The allow-list is empty at VM-0.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The allow-list is empty at VM-0, so any profile reference violates it.

rules.statement: Broiler.VM.Abstractions and Broiler.VM.Binary reference nothing outside the framework. The mechanical form of roadmap section 5's arrow to nothing.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Both assemblies are built at VM-0; the test assembly is the witness input.

rules.statement: Broiler.VM.Runtime references nothing outside Broiler.VM.Abstractions and Broiler.VM.Binary.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Broiler.VM.Runtime now uses types from both Abstractions and Binary - its meter implements Broiler.VM.IVmBoundedAllocationMeter and its verification path drives VmBoundedReader - so its AssemblyRef table names both and the rule is equality rather than subset.

rules.statement: No assembly in the product graph names a Broiler.* assembly outside the component's own set. The assembly-level twin of A1 and A2.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: A product assembly could name a foreign Broiler.* assembly. The subject now exists - the product graph names non-framework assemblies for the first time - but a VIOLATION is still unreachable: A1 forbids the outbound ProjectReference, A2 forbids the Broiler.* PackageReference, and the single-source NuGet.config makes such a package unresolvable, so no project in the checkout can acquire one. It becomes reachable at VM-3, when composition roots and profile packages exist. Exclusion EX-40 records the reasoning and the alternative that was rejected.
rules.witness: none - a witness needs a foreign Broiler assembly, and the graph is closed over its own seven. The project-file twins A1 and A2 are witnessed.

rules.statement: No exported member of a product assembly names a type outside System.* and Broiler.VM.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The product graph exports a contract surface whose members carry parameter and return types, so a foreign type on the public surface is now expressible.

rules.statement: No assembly in the product graph references a dynamic-loading, reflection-invocation or IL-emit API. Invariant 2 requires registration to be static and typed.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The witness is compiled into the test assembly, which the same scanner flags when pointed at it.

rules.statement: No assembly in the product graph applies ModuleInitializerAttribute. Invariant 2 forbids a module-initializer ordering dependency by name.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The product graph now declares method bodies, so a method could carry the attribute.

rules.statement: No product assembly references an assembly built from src/tests/.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: ApiBaselineWitnesses.FixtureReferenceWitness names a type from Broiler.VM.Fixtures - which is built from src/tests/ - so the test assembly emits the AssemblyRef the rule scans for. A project reference alone emits nothing: the compiler records only what is used, so without a real use the scanner would be pointed at an assembly that does not in fact hold the forbidden edge.

rules.statement: No product assembly exports a type named BuiltInProfiles, DefaultProfiles, AllProfiles or KnownProfiles. Roadmap section 3 rejects an aggregate profile type by name.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The product graph exports types other than VmCoreContract, so an aggregate profile type is now expressible.

rules.statement: dotnet pack over Broiler.VM.slnx produces exactly three .nupkg and three .snupkg, named for the three product assemblies.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: A component CI pack step exists. VM-0 creates no CI workflow; a manually executed pack log is retained in the evidence bundle as observed state, not as a rule assertion.

rules.statement: No produced .nuspec declares a dependency on a Broiler.* package outside the declared three.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: A component CI pack step exists.

rules.statement: No produced .nuspec's id, title, description, tags or release notes names a language. Implements roadmap section 14's packaging failure 'a language capability implied by package or API'.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: A component CI pack step exists.

rules.statement: No project file outside the component declares a ProjectReference or PackageReference resolving into Broiler.VM. The inbound half of the legacy boundary.
rules.evidence: Project files in an aggregate checkout above the component
rules.nonVacuousWhen: An aggregate checkout is present above the component root. Where none is, the rule reports INCONCLUSIVE rather than passing. Exclusion EX-01 records the conditionality.

rules.statement: VmCoreContract.Version and VmCoreContract.MinimumSupportedVersion equal the values in ADR 0003's header fields.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: ADR 0003 and VmCoreContract both exist at VM-0.

rules.statement: Every ADR file declares a Core contract header field, and the contract-bearing set is exactly 0002 through 0011.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Twelve ADR files exist at VM-0.

rules.statement: Every contract-bearing ADR declares the current core contract version.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Ten contract-bearing ADRs exist at VM-0.

rules.statement: The ADR index lists exactly the ADR files present, and every rule identifier named in an ADR has exactly one row in this register.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Twelve ADR files and this register exist at VM-0.

rules.statement: SUPERSEDED AT VM-1 by V1 and V2. As written it fused a cardinality claim about the graph (exactly one public type) with a member claim about one type (whose only members are the two contract-version constants). VM-1 necessarily falsifies the first and preserves the second. V1 replaces the cardinality half with an API baseline; V2 preserves the member half verbatim. The row is retained rather than removed so the supersession is auditable, and it asserts nothing.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Never again in this form; VM-6 owns removing the row when it freezes the public API.

rules.statement: The product graph exports every name the frozen public-name table fixes, and every exported type is declared in namespace Broiler.VM.
rules.evidence: Exported types against the frozen name baseline
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The product graph exports a contract surface. Replaces the cardinality half of E5. The witness points the rule at a graph exporting only the bounded-reading primitives which contains none of the frozen names.

rules.statement: VmCoreContract exports exactly Version and MinimumSupportedVersion, and both are literals.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: VmCoreContract exists. Preserves the member half of E5 verbatim.

rules.statement: No exported type or member uses a retired name, a struck bound name, or one of the six unqualified names the terminology rule bans.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The product graph exports a surface on which a retired name could appear.

rules.statement: VmProfileDescriptor declares exactly the thirty rows of the frozen table, by name, and none of the names excluded by construction.
rules.evidence: Compiled metadata against the frozen row list
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The descriptor exists as a type with properties. The rule compares row NAMES, not a count: a count is satisfied by any thirty-one properties at all, including thirty-one wrong ones, which is exactly the drift a table this long exists to catch.

rules.statement: Every reason in the registry maps to exactly one outcome category, derivably from its own value.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: VmReason and VmReasonRegistry exist. The witness is a reason value filed outside every category block which the derived mapping must reject.

rules.statement: The profile-facing metering surface declares exactly TryCharge, Poll, ReportRetained and ReportReleased, the charge amount is unsigned, and no member reads a remaining or effective value.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: IVmMeter exists.

rules.statement: No member on any exported type is named Grant, Refund, Reset, Extend, Increase, Raise, TopUp, Widen, Reopen, WithLimits, Withdraw or Credit.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The product graph exports members on which such a name could appear.

rules.statement: No public member returns Task, ValueTask or IAsyncEnumerable, and no product assembly calls a timer, delay or thread-abort API.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The product graph exports members with return types and declares method bodies.

rules.statement: Exactly one public member of the product graph mints a verified artifact, exactly one product assembly reaches that member, and the verification member takes exactly the descriptor, the byte span and a cancellation token.
rules.evidence: Compiled metadata: exported members, MemberRef tables, and the verification signature
rules.nonVacuousWhen: VmVerifiedArtifact and VmRuntime.Verify exist. Two halves, because either alone is weaker than the claim: counting members that return the handle would pass a graph with one factory and any number of assemblies calling it, and reading the member-reference tables says which assemblies can reach the factory at all. Neither half counts individual call sites, which would need an IL decoder; Exclusion EX-51 records that limit rather than letting the statement overreach.

rules.statement: No public member can express a persisted envelope, streaming or incremental verification, lazy per-section verification, or in-process producer input.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The product graph exports a surface on which such a member could appear.
